r.u: Turn it face-down and forget about it

r: A fully established Kashtira field is extremely tough to play through, and many Duelists are finding ways to simply flip them face-down and play through them. There’s a variety of options here, and we’ve seen them all.
is the original, and it has seen play for years because it’s a powerful and straightforward effect. Simply flip one thing down and disrupt your opponent’s plans. This can prevent
or

from attacking on their turn, or from using their effects when you use yours. You can also let your opponent begin making moves toward an Xyz Summon, then flip just one of the intended materials face-down to interrupt the play. As a Quick-Play Spell,
is solid whether you’re going first or second.
is the next step up. It flips
face-down, making it much better when going second, and still strong going first. However, it has a pretty notable downside of giving your opponent some free cards. If you’re using
to open yourself up for other plays, you may be able to destroy your opponent’s monsters before they flip up in the End Phase.
is kind of a middle ground between the first two. It hits multiple monsters like Eclipse, but without the risk of giving your opponent free cards.
has a different downside, in that it requires a discard. Of course, Duelists will realize that a discard is often no downside at all.

is the only Trap Card we’re listing here. The various Books all are Quick-Play Spells and thus very versatile, while Karma Cannon requires committing a turn to Set it. The effect can be well worth it though, as it flips everything face-down while also clearing out Link Monsters and Token Cards that would normally be unaffected.
Special shoutout to Ninjas! They have
to permanently lock monsters face-down, and they can use Jioh or any of the aforementioned cards with
to Tribute opposing monsters. They can also take advantage of turning their own monsters face-down to get the effects of cards like
. Any Deck might want to use the cards mentioned in this section, but Ninjas are the most poised to push them to the next level. To see this in action, check out our Round 6 Feature Match!
